transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I'm... I'm here because I've been trying to prove something for the past year, and it's just exhausting me. It's about my dad's lab results. I'm a phlebotomist, you know, so I draw blood all day. I see the tubes, I know the labels, I know how the system works. And someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of his results. 

I actually started working in phlebotomy because I liked the uniform, if you can believe that. The scrubs are so comfortable. I used to work retail and standing in those stiff pants all day was just awful for my knees. My sister works retail too, over at the mall, but she gets a discount on shoes, so I guess that's a perk. 

Anyway, no matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me his numbers are fine, I know what I saw. The chart doesn't match the reality of it. And it's just wearing me down, trying to get anyone to listen to me.
Have you ever heard, seen, or smelled things that others around you did not seem to notice?

No, I haven't. I mean, my hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, I had my hearing tested a few years ago when I thought I was getting ear infections. Turns out it was just allergies. The pollen around here gets so bad in the spring, doesn't it? My car is just covered in yellow dust by April. I have to run it through the car wash twice a week. I tried parking under the carport, but my neighbor keeps leaving his trash cans right in the way. He's got this old basset hound that howls all night, too. But no, I don't hear or see anything that isn't really there. I just see what they're doing to the lab results.
When you are speaking with others, do they ever tell you that your thoughts are hard to follow or that what you are saying doesn't make sense?

No, not really. People usually understand me just fine. I mean, my mom says I talk too fast sometimes, but that's just because I have a lot to say, especially when I'm trying to explain the lab stuff. She's always been a slow talker, though. She grew up in Georgia, so she's got that real slow, Southern drawl. We went down there to visit my aunt last summer, and it was so hot. The humidity just ruins my hair. I tried this new anti-frizz serum, but it smelled like coconuts, and I just can't stand coconut. It reminds me of this horrible piña colada I had at a work party once. Our clinic manager always insists on having these luau-themed parties in the middle of winter. It's so tacky. But anyway, no, I think I make perfect sense. It's just that people don't *want* to understand what's happening with the charts.
Do you feel that there is a specific person or group of people who are intentionally working against you or trying to harm you by manipulating these records?

Well, I don't know if it's one specific person or like a whole group of them, but someone is definitely doing it. I mean, it has to be someone with access to the electronic medical records system, right? We use Epic at my clinic, and let me tell you, when we first switched over from the old system, it was a nightmare. We had these trainers come in, and they were wearing these bright purple polo shirts. Purple is just not my color. I bought a purple sweater once, thinking it would bring out my eyes, but it just made me look washed out. My sister said I looked like a bruised plum. She can be so mean sometimes. She's the one who works at the mall, remember? Anyway, she borrowed my favorite denim jacket last month and still hasn't given it back. I was going to wear it to this outdoor concert last weekend, but I had to wear a cardigan instead, and it just wasn't the same vibe. The band was okay, but the lead singer kept messing up the lyrics to their biggest hit. Like, how do you forget your own song? But yeah, I don't know exactly who is doing it, but they're definitely doing it on purpose to hide the truth about my dad's numbers.
Have you ever found yourself unable to move, or have you ever acted in ways that others found strange or bizarre?

Unable to move? No, never. And I don't act strange or bizarre either. I mean, I'm on my feet all day drawing blood, so I'm constantly moving around the clinic. Actually, I just had to buy these new compression socks because my calves were absolutely killing me by the end of my shift. I found this pair online that has little avocados all over them. They're super cute, but they took forever to ship. I ordered them on a Tuesday, and they didn't get here until, like, the following Thursday. 

The mail carrier in my neighborhood is just terrible, though. He always leaves my packages on the bottom step instead of bringing them up to the porch, and last time it rained, my whole FabFitFun box got completely soaked. All the cardboard just turned to mush. It was so annoying because there was this really expensive vitamin C serum in there that I was dying to try. My skin has been so dry lately with the weather changing. I tried using that heavy CeraVe cream, but it just makes my face feel greasy, you know? It gets all over my pillowcases. I just bought these silk pillowcases, too, because I read they're better for preventing wrinkles. But anyway, no, I don't freeze up or do anything weird. I just go to work and do my job.
Aside from the lab results regarding your father, are there any other situations where you feel that people or systems are working against you or hiding the truth from you?

No, I don't think so. It's really just the lab records with my dad. I mean, my cable company is definitely a rip-off, but that's just normal corporate greed, you know? They keep raising my bill by like five dollars every month without telling me. I tried calling them on Tuesday, and I was on hold for forty-five minutes. And they have that terrible hold music—that smooth jazz that sounds like it's playing underwater? It gave me such a horrible headache. 

I ended up having to take some Advil and just lie down on the couch. I usually prefer Tylenol, but the CVS near my apartment was completely out of the name brand, and I just don't trust the generic. My friend Sarah says the generic is exactly the same because of FDA rules or whatever, but she also thinks it's okay to put pineapple on pizza, so I don't really trust her judgment on much these days. We actually went to this artisanal pizza place downtown for her birthday last weekend, and it was so loud in there I couldn't even hear myself think. They had all these exposed pipes and Edison bulbs everywhere, which I guess is supposed to look industrial and trendy, but it just made the lighting super weird and harsh. It totally washed me out in all the pictures we took. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, people hiding things. No, it's just the clinic charts. Everything else is pretty normal.
How long have you been certain that someone is tampering with your father's lab results?

Well, it's been about a year now. Yeah, pretty much right around the time his medical problems started and he needed all those frequent labs and appointments. I was actually the one who took him to his first specialist appointment because my mom had jury duty that week. She was so annoyed about it, too, because she had just started this new water aerobics class at the Y, and she didn't want to miss it. The instructor is this guy named Todd who apparently plays 80s pop music the whole time. My mom loves Madonna. She actually still has her original cassette tape of Like a Virgin. Can you believe that? I don't even know where you'd find a cassette player these days. 

I guess maybe at a thrift store? I went to one a couple of weeks ago looking for a vintage mirror for my hallway, but all they had were these really tacky lamps with the fringe on the shades. Who buys those? They just collect dust. And dust is the absolute worst for my allergies. I've been sneezing non-stop since the pollen count went up. I tried taking Claritin, but it makes me so sleepy I can barely keep my eyes open at work. I almost dropped a whole tray of vacutainers the other day. My supervisor would have killed me. She's already on edge because we're short-staffed since Brenda went on maternity leave. Brenda had a little boy, by the way. She named him Jaxon, with an 'x'. I just think that's going to be so confusing for him when he learns to spell. But yeah, it's been going on for a year, ever since all his appointments started.

I have noticed that when we talk, your mind often jumps to many different, unrelated topics; do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing or that you have trouble keeping your mind on one specific subject?

Racing thoughts? No, not really. I mean, I don't feel like my mind is going a mile a minute or anything. I just have a lot going on, you know? Like, I'm trying to plan my sister's baby shower right now, and it's honestly taking up so much brain space. She wants this whole woodland creature theme, which is cute in theory, but finding little fox and raccoon decorations that don't look cheap or creepy is actually really hard. I went to Party City last week, and all their stuff looked like it was from a dollar store. 

And speaking of the dollar store, I actually found these amazing little glass jars there the other day. I bought like twenty of them because I want to start meal-prepping overnight oats. I saw this TikTok where this girl made them with chia seeds and almond milk and fresh berries, and it looked so good. I'm trying to eat healthier because the vending machine at the clinic is just full of junk. It's all Doritos and Honey Buns. The other day, I got a bag of pretzels, and they were completely stale. The expiration date said 2022! Can you believe they'd leave something in there that long? It's so unsanitary. 

But anyway, no, I don't have trouble focusing. I just have a lot of details to keep track of, between work and the shower and everything else.
Do you find that you have lost interest in being around your friends or family, or do you find it difficult to experience pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

No, I still like seeing my friends and family. I mean, I just mentioned I'm planning my sister's baby shower, right? I'm actually really excited about it, even if the decorations are stressing me out. We're going to have this little hot chocolate bar with different kinds of marshmallows and those chocolate stirring spoons. I found a recipe online to make them myself because the ones at the gourmet shop downtown were like four dollars each, which is just ridiculous for a piece of chocolate on a wooden stick. 

I bought the sticks at Michael's the other day. I love going in there, honestly, it always smells like cinnamon brooms and fake flowers, which reminds me of my grandma's house. She used to make these massive floral wreaths for every single season. She had this one for Halloween that was just covered in these tiny plastic spiders, and it used to terrify my brother when we were little. He would literally cry if he had to walk past the front door. He's still afraid of spiders, actually. He found a wolf spider in his garage last month and made his wife go out and deal with it. She used a broom to sweep it outside. 

I don't mind spiders, but I cannot stand centipedes. They have way too many legs, it's just unnatural. I saw one in the breakroom at the clinic last week, right near the biohazard bins. I told the janitor, but he just shrugged. He's always so unhelpful. But no, I still enjoy doing things and seeing people. Everything is fine with that.
